title: Management Portal
subtitle: Ops command center replacing 200+ spreadsheets with real-time intelligence.
metaDescription: LLM-powered ops command center for Wisdom — replaced 200+ spreadsheets with real-time A/R intelligence, designed to support a 260→900 office scale.
role: Lead Product Designer — Strategy & UX Architecture
challenge: Wisdom's ops team managed 260+ offices across 9 Team Leads using 200+ interconnected Google Sheets. Risk was invisible until it became a crisis — at-risk clients were caught too late, capacity was opaque, and manual reconciliation was creating payroll and billing errors.
approach: Designed a centralized Management Portal as an ops command center. Built an LLM-powered Office Watchlist that detects A/R aging signals and ranks offices by urgency before issues escalate. Added workforce capacity views, per-specialist performance tracking, centralized profiles, and executive portfolio dashboards — replacing manual PDFs and spreadsheets with in-app reporting.
outcome: Platform in development for Q1–Q2 2026 rollout. Designed to support 260→900 office scale, achieve 90%+ WAU among Team Leads, reduce churn from 1.8% to below 1.0%, and decommission 200+ operational spreadsheets. Shifts the ops model from reactive firefighting to proactive risk management.

body.text: Overview

Wisdom’s operations organization had outgrown its tooling. At 260+ managed offices, teams relied on 200+ interconnected Google Sheets to track performance, risk, and workforce activity — creating blind spots, delays, and operational risk.
This project focused on redefining how operations sees the business by designing a unified Management Portal that replaces fragmented reporting with real-time operational intelligence.
My Role

I led the strategy and experience design for Management Portal, working closely with Operations, Finance, and Engineering leadership. This wasn’t a UI refresh—it was a rethinking of how information flows through the organization.
My focus was on:

items: Defining the product vision and problem space
Mapping operational workflows and breakdowns
Designing systems for risk detection, capacity planning, and performance tracking
Creating experience flows and dashboards that support different roles
Aligning design decisions with real operational constraints

body.text: The result is a foundation for an internal platform designed to scale with the business.
The Challenge
As Wisdom scaled, the operations model didn’t scale with it.

By the end of 2025, Operations was managing 260+ offices across 9 Team Leads, with plans to grow to 900+. But the systems supporting that work were built for a much smaller organization. Nearly everything depended on a fragile network of 200+ interconnected Google Sheets that were slow, hard to maintain, and increasingly unreliable.

body.alt: Diagram of a Team Lead at the centre of five disconnected sources — alerts, specialist activity, a communication board, profiles and reports — linked by manual search, data hunting, multiple clicks, tab switching and fragmented access
body.caption: Leads spend hours daily assembling reports from multiple sources (Google sheets)

body.text: This created a compounding set of problems across the organization:
At-Risk Clients Were Identified Too Late

The strongest churn signals—rising A/R aging and declining collections—were buried across spreadsheets. Team Leads often didn’t realize an office was in trouble until aging had already spiked or the client escalated. There was no true early-warning system, no trend visibility, and no shared prioritization model.
An increasing over-90 balance is a red flag. We need a proactive approach to client management, not something we discover after it’s already a problem.
No Clear View of Team Load or Capacity

Team Leads had no reliable way to see how work was distributed across Revenue Specialists. Assignments were assessed manually by scanning long lists in spreadsheets, making it difficult to spot burnout, over-assignment, or unused capacity. As a result, some specialists were stretched too thin while others were underutilized—without leadership having a clear view of either.
Information about biller performance and office assignments is scattered across too many places. It’s hard to understand capacity or bandwidth.
Revenue Specialist Performance Was Hard to Track

Understanding how a Revenue Specialist was performing across multiple office assignments required jumping between tabs, sheets, and tools. Activity, output, and progress weren’t visible in one place, which meant issues surfaced weeks late and strong performance often went unrecognized.
Manual Data Entry Across Disconnected Systems

Critical office and workforce data lived in multiple places. Information like Tax IDs, NPIs, logins, assignments, and onboarding details were copied and pasted across systems, increasing the risk of errors and slowing down onboarding. There was no single source of truth for office or workforce profiles.
We spend too much time manually entering and reconciling data. It introduces errors and slows everything down.
Sales & GTM Execution Was Largely Invisible

Leadership lacked visibility into how services were being used, added, or upgraded over time. This made it difficult to validate pricing models, understand expansion opportunities, or connect operational performance to go-to-market decisions.
Reporting Was Manual, Fragmented, and Risky

Reporting relied on manual exports and reconciliation, introducing errors and delays. Payroll, invoicing, and audits were harder than they needed to be, and leadership didn’t have real-time insight into cash flow or operational performance. In some cases, the volume of data caused tools to crash entirely, increasing financial risk.
The volume of data causes our tools to lag or crash, which puts us at risk of payroll and billing mistakes.
The Core Problem
Across all of these issues, the root cause was the same:
Operations was forced to react to problems instead of anticipating them.
The challenge wasn’t just to centralize data—but to design a system that surfaces risk early, supports better decisions, and can scale with the business without adding operational overhead

body.alt: Management Portal command centre: a team lead dashboard combining the Office Watchlist, company performance table, PAR scores and collections trends in one view

body.text: The Solution

Management Portal was designed as a centralized operations command center—a single place where teams could quickly understand what’s happening, where attention is needed, and what actions to take next.
Rather than building one-off dashboards, the system focuses on surfacing early signals and reducing the effort it takes to stay informed.
Early Risk Detection (Office Watchlist, LLM-powered early risk detection)

I designed an Office Watchlist powered by an LLM that continuously evaluates aging signals and flags offices when A/R aging crosses defined thresholds (ex: over-60 / over-90 balances, rapid week-over-week changes, and sustained negative collection trends).
Instead of Team Leads digging through spreadsheets to “find the fire,” the Watchlist:

items: Detects risk states automatically as thresholds are hit (and as trends accelerate)
Ranks offices by urgency so attention goes to the highest-impact issues first
Explains the “why” (what changed, which threshold triggered, what’s trending)
Keeps humans in control (Team Leads validate, take action, and add context)

body.text: The result: a true early-warning system that surfaces issues weeks earlier than manual monitoring—without turning the product into another noisy dashboard
How it worked:
Data in → signal out:

items: Inputs: aging buckets, collections trend, office metadata, staffing/assignment context
Logic: LLM + rules-based thresholds (guardrails)
Output: risk state + explanation + recommended next step

body.title: Why LLM, not just rules
items: Rules catch “threshold hit.”
The LLM adds the missing layer: pattern recognition + summarization (what changed, how fast, what’s anomalous, what to look at next), so Team Leads don’t waste time interpreting raw data.

body.alt: Office Watchlist flagging three critical offices with the reason for each — 90-day aging spiked 12% week over week, collection ratio at 65% — beside aging buckets, PAR score and the assigned team lead, poster and ager
body.caption: Automated risk states surface issues weeks earlier the current manual monitoring and reporting.

body.text: Workforce & Capacity Visibility

To address burnout and underutilization, I introduced clear views into Revenue Specialist workload and capacity. This makes it easier to balance assignments and understand where teams are stretched—or where there’s room to take on more.

body.alt: Revenue specialist roster showing availability, start date, practice management system, PAR score and per-skill coverage across posting, aging, patient aging and insurance verification
body.caption: Capacity-aware views reduce burnout and unlock underutilized output.

body.text: Performance Tracking

Each Revenue Specialist has a dedicated view that shows how they’re performing across assignments. This gives Team Leads better context for coaching, feedback, and recognition without creating a culture of micromanagement.

body.alt: An individual revenue specialist's performance view: PAR score against benchmark, average days in A/R, recent activity, and collections broken down by aging category
body.caption: Performance visibility without micromanagement.

body.text: Centralized Profiles & Data
Office and Revenue Specialist information is now centralized. Data is entered once and reused across the system, reducing manual errors and making onboarding and day-to-day operations much smoother.

body.alt: Centralized office profile for Sunrise Dental showing office information and linked provider records in a single editable record
body.caption: Enter data once. Use it everywhere.

body.text: Executive Visibility
Leadership gets portfolio-level and company-wide views that surface trends, risk, and usage without having to request reports or pull data from multiple tools.
In-App Reporting
Manual PDFs and spreadsheets were replaced with in-app reporting and production tracking. This improves accuracy for payroll and invoicing and gives Finance better real-time visibility.

body.alt: In-app monthly reporting: office production and collections by month with gross production, write-offs, net production and collection rate, exportable to CSV
body.caption: Manual reporting replaced with real-time visibility

body.alt: Offices roster showing onboarding, assignment and live status per office, beside an office detail view listing team lead, posting, aging and insurance verification assignments

body.text: Results & Impact (Projected)

Management Portal is currently in development, with planned rollout across Q1–Q2 2026. The outcomes below reflect the intended impact of the platform based on defined goals, operational baselines, and leadership alignment.
Reducing Preventable Customer Churn

One of the primary goals of Management Portal is to reduce customer churn driven by insufficient revenue collection. As of Q4 2025, Wisdom’s churn rate sits at 1.8%, with aging A/R and declining collections being the most common early indicators of churn.

Management Portal is designed to surface these signals earlier—before they escalate into client complaints or cancellations—through automated office watchlists and risk states. By giving Team Leads clear, prioritized visibility into offices that are trending in the wrong direction, the platform enables earlier intervention and more proactive client management.
Projected impact:

items: Reduce churn from 1.8% to below 1.0%
Identify at-risk offices weeks earlier through aging and collections trends
Shift churn prevention from reactive to proactive

body.text: Improving Data Transparency & Adoption
Today, Team Leads and Managers rely heavily on layered Google Sheets to understand performance, workload, and risk. This slows decision-making and creates dependency on manual reporting.

Management Portal centralizes this information into a single system designed for daily use. The goal is not just visibility, but adoption—making the portal the first place Team Leads go to understand what’s happening across their portfolio.
Projected impact:

items: Decommission or significantly reduce reliance on operational spreadsheets
Achieve 90%+ Weekly Active Usage (WAU) among Team Leads
Faster access to trusted data without manual reconciliation

body.text: Increasing Team Lead Efficiency While Maintaining NPS

As the business scales, operational efficiency must improve without sacrificing service quality. Wisdom’s NPS was 73.47 as of Q3, exceeding the target of 70+, but maintaining that score becomes harder as office count grows.

Management Portal is designed to reduce the cognitive and manual load on Team Leads by eliminating hours of data hunting and replacing it with clear, prioritized views. This allows Team Leads to spend more time supporting offices and less time assembling reports.
Projected impact:

items: Improved Team Lead efficiency and sustainability
Maintain or exceed 70+ NPS as office count increases
Support higher office-to-Team Lead ratios without burnout

body.text: Supporting Workload Balance & Team Satisfaction

Another key goal is improving overall satisfaction for Team Leads and Revenue Specialists while preparing the organization to scale to 900 offices by EOY. Without visibility into workload and capacity, teams risk burnout on one end and underutilization on the other.
Management Portal introduces clear workload and performance visibility across Revenue Specialists, helping leadership make better assignment decisions and spot issues before they compound.
Projected impact:

items: Better workload balance across Revenue Specialists
Increased Team Lead confidence in assignments and performance
Tooling designed to support growth from 260 → 900 offices without linear increases in operational overhead

body.text: Summary

Management Portal is not positioned as a quick fix—it is foundational infrastructure. The platform is being built to help Wisdom operate more proactively, reduce preventable churn, maintain service quality at scale, and give teams the clarity they need to make better decisions every day.
By the time it launches, success won’t be measured by dashboards alone—but by how effectively teams can anticipate problems, act earlier, and scale without losing control.

title: Posting Assistant
subtitle: AI-assisted insurance payment posting workflow that kept specialists in control.
metaDescription: AI-assisted insurance payment posting workflow that cut manual time by 40%, keeping specialists in control while automating repetitive reconciliation.
challenge: Insurance payment posting was chaotic — documents came in every format, specialists jumped between screens comparing EOBs, and every posting required manual judgment calls. Slow, error-prone, and impossible to scale.
approach: Instead of jumping to full automation, started with an assistive workflow: OCR + LLMs extracted key data from scanned insurance documents and surfaced it in a structured review interface. Preserved specialist control while reducing cognitive load. Used OBS Studio to run observational research across multiple monitors. Once trust was established, integrated with Open Dental for deeper automation.
outcome: 40% reduction in manual posting time. Transformed a messy multi-screen workflow into a structured AI-assisted tool. Created a path to scale without adding headcount, and a strong foundation for full automation in the next phase.

body.text: Posting Assistant was built to help Wisdom’s revenue specialists process insurance payments faster and with less manual work. We used OCR and LLMs to parse scanned EOBs, payment docs, and denial details, then surfaced that information in a structured workflow that made posting easier and faster. Later, we integrated with Open Dental, which helped reduce manual posting time by 40%.
Key impact

items: Reduced manual posting time by 40%
Conducted 40+ user interviews for Posting Assistant
Turned a messy multi-screen workflow into a structured AI-assisted tool
Helped create a path from manual assistive tooling to deeper automation

body.alt: Service blueprint of the payment posting journey, mapping the dental office's document upload against the biller's steps inside Wisdom, ending at the office's practice management system
body.caption: The posting journey mapped end to end, from the office uploading documents to the biller working them inside Wisdom.

body.text: The challenge
Payment posting was one of those workflows that looked simple from the outside, but once you really got into it, it was messy and time-consuming.

Insurance documents came in all kinds of formats. Some were clean, some were hard to read, some had missing context, and a lot of them required interpretation. Revenue specialists had to look through the document, figure out what happened, understand why something was or wasn’t paid, and then manually enter that information into another system.

It was a very manual process, and it also required a lot of attention to detail. People were constantly switching between screens, comparing information, and making judgment calls. That made the work slower, harder to scale, and more mentally draining than it needed to be.
We saw an opportunity to make that whole process better by extracting the important information up front and giving specialists a workflow that supported the way they already worked.
My role

I led the design of Posting Assistant end to end, from discovery and workflow definition through prototyping, interface design, and iteration. I worked closely with product and engineering, conducted user research, and helped define how we would measure the workflow before and after launch.

I also set up observational research using OBS Studio so we could watch revenue specialists work across multiple monitors in their real environment and understand where time and effort were being lost.
Approach

Instead of jumping straight to full automation, we started with an assistive workflow. OCR and LLMs extracted key information from scanned insurance documents, and the product surfaced that information in a way revenue specialists could quickly review and act on.
This approach helped us:

items: reduce cognitive load
support trust in AI-generated output
preserve specialist control in a complex workflow
create a foundation for deeper automation later

body.text: Once the workflow proved value, we extended it through Open Dental integration, which removed more manual work and drove a meaningful time savings.

body.alt: File intake form capturing deposit totals and scan counts, alongside the Post to Open Dental patient search used to match a payment to the correct record
body.caption: Intake captures the deposit once; posting to Open Dental matches the payment to a patient record without leaving the workflow.

body.alt: Check detail for a $50,000 Delta Dental payment showing nine paid claims and nine still waiting to post, with submitted amount, patient responsibility and plan payment per patient
body.caption: Claim-level detail for a single check, showing what has posted and what still needs attention.

body.text: Impact
Reduced manual posting time by around 40%
The biggest outcome was the reduction in manual posting time. Once we introduced the product and later integrated with Open Dental, we were able to cut manual posting time by about 40%.
Made the workflow easier on the team

The product reduced how much specialists had to manually read, interpret, and re-enter on every task. Instead of starting from a blank slate every time, they were working from structured information that was already surfaced for them.
Created a path to scale without adding headcount
By making the workflow more efficient, Posting Assistant helped the team handle more volume without relying on more manual effort to get there.
Built a stronger foundation for future automation
The first version helped prove the value and establish trust. That made it possible to keep improving the experience and automate more over time.

title: Page Builder 2.0
subtitle: CRM page builder rebuilt from scratch in 2 months to stop churn from competitors.
metaDescription: Rebuilt Simplero's CRM page builder from scratch in 2 months — WYSIWYG editing and competitor import drove a 9% post-launch sales increase.
challenge: Users found Simplero's page builder so limiting they resorted to custom CSS and were threatening to migrate to competitors. The old builder prevented migration from other platforms and was driving churn.
approach: Led the full redesign from scratch: user and expert interviews, competitive analysis, product requirements (no PM — I owned that role), and close collaboration with the Lead Engineer to ship fast. Delivered a WYSIWYG editor, style guide, color picker, and competitor page import — all in 2 months.
outcome: 9% increase in sales post-launch. Customer migration increased. Engineers shipped with minimal friction. Users who previously exported to external developers stayed on platform. Positioned Simplero as a credible CRM platform, not just a tool.

body.text: Overview

In response to mounting user dissatisfaction with Simplero's outdated page builder, I led the redesign and implementation of a revolutionary solution within Simplero's CRM system. The primary goal was to overcome the limitations of the existing builder, which users found clunky and restrictive, leading some to resort to custom CSS and even contemplate leaving the platform. My role involved conducting extensive user and expert interviews, creating product requirements, and collaborating closely with the Lead Engineer to bring about a transformative change. The result was a feature-rich page builder with innovative elements such as a WYSIWYG editor, style guide, color picker, and more.
My role

As the lead product designer, I spearheaded the entire redesign process, from conducting user and expert interviews to creating comprehensive product requirements. In the absence of a product manager, I took charge of outlining the project's goals and collaborated closely with the Lead Engineer to ensure seamless integration of design and functionality. My responsibilities included a comprehensive competitive analysis, design and architecture of innovative features, and the production of various design artifacts such as personas, sketches, wireframes, UI designs, and prototypes. Throughout the process, I played a pivotal role in enhancing the overall user experience and addressing critical pain points within Simplero's CRM system.

body.alt: Style guide artboard for the page builder covering colour palettes and pickers, font pairing selection, buttons, form fields and borders, with a rendered style-guide preview
body.caption: The style system behind the builder: colour, type, buttons and form fields defined once so every page inherits them.

body.text: The Challenge

body.alt: The previous page builder: a text panel offering only style, width, padding and background controls, beside the landing page it renders
body.caption: The old page builder was limited in customization

body.text: The project aimed to address critical issues with Simplero's existing page builder. Users faced challenges in achieving their desired designs, resorting to external developers and custom CSS. Migration from other platforms was hindered, and the threat of user exodus loomed. The primary target was to enhance user satisfaction and retention. The challenge involved understanding user needs, conducting a comprehensive competitive analysis, and formulating product requirements. Technical constraints and the need for efficient design were crucial considerations to ensure a streamlined development process.

body.alt: Landing pages being edited in the new builder — a funnel marketing page, a post-purchase thank-you page, a popup editor and an appointment booking page
body.caption: Real customer pages in the new editor, including popups and booking flows rather than only marketing pages.

body.text: The Solution: Empowering CRM Excellence through Simplero’s Page Builder Revolution

The redesign journey commenced with in-depth user and expert interviews, unraveling frustrations with Simplero's existing page builder. This insight shaped detailed product requirements, where, in the absence of a dedicated product manager, I assumed a lead role in defining project goals. A comprehensive competitive analysis not only spotlighted the flaws in Simplero's builder but also drew inspiration from industry-leading features, setting the redesign's trajectory.

Collaboration with the Lead Engineer ensured a seamless fusion of design and functionality, resulting in a swift and efficient development process. The innovative features, including a WYSIWYG editor, style guide, color picker, and more, were meticulously crafted to empower users, addressing customization needs and enhancing the overall design flexibility. Crucially, the redesign underscored the symbiotic relationship between a robust page builder and CRM users.

Recognizing the pivotal role of CRM integration, the new design seamlessly incorporated the page builder into Simplero's CRM system. This strategic move aimed not only to rectify clunkiness but to position Simplero as a CRM platform leader. The redesign was more than a fix; it was a statement of empowerment, customer loyalty, and an elevated market standing. In essence, the project highlighted the vital role a sophisticated page builder plays in enhancing the broader CRM user experience.

body.alt: Input field configuration showing format and advanced tabs, selection from existing CRM fields such as birth date and contact email, and the list of new field types that can be added
body.caption: Settings for inputs

body.alt: Colour management in the builder: the palette, custom colours, and four named colour styles previewed against sample page content
body.caption: Named colour styles let a customer restyle a whole page without editing each block.

body.text: Results
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):
Enhanced Customer Satisfaction:

items: Customer satisfaction witnessed a significant improvement post-implementation of the new page builder.

body.text: Increased Customer Migration:

items: Users are now eager to migrate their entire websites to Simplero, predicting a subsequent increase in the lifetime value of customers.

body.text: Efficient Development Process:

items: Engineers encountered minimal barriers during the building phase, leading to the quick deployment of the new page builder within months.

body.text: Competitor Page Imports:

items: Users can now seamlessly import pages from competitors' builders, expanding Simplero's ecosystem and attracting users from other platforms.

body.text: Conclusion

Post-implementation, the project yielded remarkable results. Customer satisfaction soared, leading to increased customer migration and a predicted rise in the lifetime value of customers. The efficient design process allowed engineers to swiftly bring the new page builder to fruition, and users can now seamlessly import pages from competitors' builders. The success of this project not only addressed critical user pain points but also showcased the power of user-centric design and collaborative innovation. As a lead product designer, the experience reinforced the importance of investing in the entire project lifecycle and continually seeking opportunities for career development.

title: Connect API Payments
subtitle: PCI Level 1 embedded payments widget shipped with $20M+ monthly volume in month one.
metaDescription: Designed Plastiq's PCI Level 1-compliant payments widget from zero — $20M+ monthly volume in month one, three enterprise partnerships secured pre-launch.
challenge: Build a PCI-compliant embedded payments widget that would let enterprise clients integrate card and ACH payments into their own platforms — while eliminating merchant fees, expanding working capital, and onboarding partners in weeks.
approach: Worked closely with the PM to define the product vision from zero. Designed an end-to-end payment widget and developer portal through iterative wireframing and expert interviews. Baked PCI Level 1 certification into the design process from day one — not as an afterthought. Partnered with Billfire, Brex, and PayGround before launch.
outcome: $20M+ monthly payment volume exceeded in the first month. Three strategic partnerships secured pre-launch. Clients consistently commented on the solidity and intuitiveness of the partner portal. Clients can get up and running in 8 weeks.

body.text: Overview

Plastiq Connect transformed API payments, crafting an end-to-end payment widget and a developer portal. Through iterative wireframing and expert interviews, the solution achieved client recognition for its solidity and intuitive design. This project sets a new standard, emphasizing security, usability, and collaborative design in shaping the future of financial transactions.

body.alt: Nearside-branded payment screens showing account balance, transfer funds, add a contact and account menu, demonstrating the widget carrying a partner’s own branding
body.caption: The widget white-labelled for Nearside: the partner’s brand, not Plastiq’s, in front of their customers.

body.text: Navigating Complexity: Designing Plastiq Connect to Tackle the Challenges of API Payments

The challenge was to create a solution that provided flexibility to payers and vendors, ensuring seamless transactions across various payment methods. Plastiq Connect aimed to eliminate merchant fees, enhance security, expedite payment processes for sellers, and allow buyers to pay vendors by card regardless of acceptance. Additionally, the project focused on expanding working capital for sellers and providing a robust framework for capturing additional revenue and insights from in-product customer payments.

body.caption: Adding a card, with saved cards and bank accounts selectable from the same list.

body.text: The solution: Crafting a Seamless Financial Ecosystem
At the epicenter of Plastiq Connect's success was a meticulous design solution, where my daily collaboration with the product manager played a pivotal role in shaping the product's vision.

body.alt: Review payment screen showing amount, fees, total, the card being charged, delivery method by wire transfer, recipient details, invoice number and memo before submitting
body.caption: Every number the payer is committing to — amount, fee, total, delivery method and recipient — on one screen before submit.

body.text: End-to-End Payment Widget and Developer Portal: A Gateway to Innovation

In close collaboration with the product manager, we set a clear vision for the product. Iterating tirelessly on wireframes, we crafted a solution that not only satisfied business needs but also ensured a seamless onboarding experience for potential clients. The design process involved countless hours of expert interviews and iteration of initial ideas and strategies. By remaining agile and respecting the collective vision of the company and potential clients, we produced a solution that stood at the intersection of innovation and usability.
Security Beyond Standards: PCI Level 1 Certification and Bank-Grade Protection

The commitment to security was not just a checkbox but an integral part of the design process. The implementation of PCI Level 1 certification and bank-grade security measures was a result of continuous iteration and expert interviews. This rigorous approach reassured our partners and users, garnering frequent comments on the solidity of the product's design.

body.text: Seamless Integration with Freedom of Choice: UI Design Excellence

The UI design was a labor of love, guided by the principles of usability and clarity. Clients frequently commented on the solid design of the product, particularly highlighting the intuitiveness of the partner portal. The portal, developed through countless iterations, provided an easy way for developers to integrate Connect into their systems, ensuring a smooth and intuitive experience.

In essence, our design solution was not just about creating a product; it was about fostering a collaborative vision, iterating tirelessly, and respecting the diverse needs of clients. Plastiq Connect's end-to-end payment widget and developer portal, coupled with stringent security measures and an intuitive UI, emerged as a testament to the success that can be achieved through a harmonious blend of collaboration, innovation, and user-centric design.

Working tirelessly alongside the product manager and business analyst, we collectively crafted a PCI-compliant end-to-end payment widget that not only met but exceeded industry standards, redefining the landscape of secure and seamless financial transactions.
